claimBoundary: The source-generated matrix crosses coding mode (baseline/progressive) with vertical-only 4:4:0 and two-axis 4:2:0 sampling. It bypasses RGB-to-YCbCr conversion and encoder chroma downsampling via libjpeg raw_data_in; Y is constant 128, Cr is constant 128, and Cb varies only by low-resolution row. The actual post-IDCT planes are re-observed with raw_data_out before model evaluation.

For each generated JPEG and backend independently, one affine blue-versus-reconstructed-Cb map is fit only on non-boundary output rows, where global and iMCU-clamped context models are identical. The frozen map is then evaluated on held-out phase-0/15 rows. libjpeg must prefer global 3/4-current + 1/4-adjacent context, while ImageCraft/ImageIO must prefer the same kernel with context clamped at 16-output-row iMCU boundaries.

If the opposite model preference appears for any coding-mode/sampling cell, the matrix fails rather than widening a tolerance. Passing both baseline and progressive cells means the observed ImageIO context behavior is not progressive-specific in this generated domain; it still does not assert knowledge of Apple's internal implementation.

The retained real-photo progressive case is an external phase-localization check only. No pixel delta, MAE, RMSE or source-generated fit becomes a public conformance tolerance or a perceptual-quality claim.
